title: O God, That Madest Earth and Sky
description: O God, That Madest Earth and Sky in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 931 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “In Times of Domestic Distress”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, that ma-dest earth and sky! The dark-ness and the day! Give ear to this thy fa-mi-ly, And help us when we pray! For wide the waves of bit-ter-ness A-round our ves-sel roar, And hea-vy grows the pi-lot's heart To view the roc-ky shore!

lines: O God, that madest earth and sky!
Give ear to this thy family,
And help us when we pray!
For wide the waves of bitterness
And heavy grows the pilot's heart
The cross our Master bore for us,
For him we fain would bear,
But mortal strength to weakness turns,
Then mercy on our failings, Lord!
And when thy sorrows visit us,

licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
